summary: Steady production throughput regression: elevated p95/p99 and request timeouts during multi-tenant burst due to VRAM paging and autoscale sensitivity
description: Issue summary: Customer Beacon HealthTech reported sudden, sustained throughput degradation and an increase in p95/p99 request latency for inference on their dedicated reservation. Multiple streaming and non-streaming requests returned 504/429 intermittently. Impact: Customer-facing API endpoints experienced timeouts affecting user-facing chat features for about 2.5 hours. Scope: Only the customer's dedicated reservation in us-west-2; other customers on the same cluster showed intermittent degradation but not full outage. Initial severity assessed as P1/Sev1.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Target Beacon's dedicated reservation in us-west-2 with high-concurrency chat workload (burst to ~200 concurrent requests). 2) Use gpt-13b-instruct-q4 model with sequences averaging 512 tokens and occasional longer tails to 1024. 3) Observe p95/p99 latency and 504/429 counts in the first 20 minutes of the burst. 4) Correlate with node vmstat/iostat and GPU memory metrics.

investigation_notes: Node-level findings: runner-34 showed VRAM fragmentation and intermittent paging when concurrent high-token sequences overlapped with background memcpy-heavy batch jobs.
Scheduler behavior: short-lived batch jobs (~30-90s) created allocation churn; scheduler rebalanced containers onto the same GPU causing temporary overcommit.

Autoscaler sensitivity: current scaling policy uses short aggregation window (30s) and a low hysteresis, causing three rapid scale actions that increased scheduling churn and reduced steady throughput during the burst.
No hardware faults found: GPU drivers and metrics didn't report ECC or hardware errors; observed behavior consistent with software-level memory reclamation under pressure.
Correlation: p95/p99 spikes lined up with background batch start times and with autoscaler scale events within +/- 20s.

Customer impact note: Beacon's reservation was configured with burstable concurrency which allowed host-sharing; their workload pattern (many medium-length requests) is particularly sensitive to VRAM fragmentation.
Related artifacts: linked monitoring dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/allocations/runner-34, scheduler trace: https://traces.redwood.internal/trace/ab12cd
resolution: Root cause: combination of noisy neighbor background batch jobs causing GPU VRAM fragmentation/paging plus an autoscaler configuration with short windows and low hysteresis that amplified scheduling churn during a traffic burst. Permanent fixes applied: 1) Adjusted autoscaler policy for dedicated reservations to use longer aggregation window (120s) and increased hysteresis to prevent oscillation. 2) Implemented host-affinity enforcement for dedicated reservations by default (migration scheduled during off-peak). 3) Added a soft QoS limiter for background batch jobs to avoid colocating high-mem-copy workloads with latency-sensitive inference. 4) Updated monitoring and alerting to detect VRAM paging and autoscale oscillation patterns. 5) Backfilled a small code change (PR #4581) to the scheduler to prefer runners with contiguous free VRAM over fragmented hosts. Follow-up actions: postmortem to be published, review of default reservation concurrency settings, and a runbook entry added to Confluence.
